source: User-approved 55-feature scope in Dvar project conversation

milestones.M1: Release hold, network foundation, shared-state and telemetry primitives
milestones.M2: Identity, ownership, delegation and operation controls
milestones.M4: MCP protocol, streaming, OAuth and supply-chain security
milestones.M5: Data classification, provenance, DLP and output contracts
milestones.M7: Python, Mayura, frameworks, presets and developer tooling
milestones.M8: Security analytics and integrated v1 qualification

features.name: Advanced URL and SSRF protection
acceptance: Validate URL parsing, credentials, every IPv4/IPv6 DNS answer and every redirect; connect only to the validated address while preserving TLS hostname verification.
Reject rebinding, mixed public/private DNS, mapped IPs, metadata endpoints, proxy bypass, unsafe fallback and timeout races across every supported outbound boundary.
remaining: Full repository CI and built-package ESM/CommonJS consumer qualification.
Integrate and qualify every supported outbound boundary; existing fetch injection is opt-in in slice 01.
Independent adversarial review and deployment-level network isolation evidence.

features.name: Network egress firewall
acceptance: Enforce explicit host, scheme, method, port and destination rules with deny precedence and narrow private-service exceptions.
Prove denied requests never connect; integrate with MCP, credential/webhook traffic and protected agent HTTP tools; document OS-level network containment separately.
remaining: Full repository CI and built-package ESM/CommonJS consumer qualification.
Integrate and qualify every supported outbound boundary; existing fetch injection is opt-in in slice 01.
Independent adversarial review and deployment-level network isolation evidence.

features.name: Sensitive operation classification
acceptance: Classify finance, database, identity, repository, infrastructure and destructive operations from trusted manifests and reviewed mappings.
Expose provenance, overrides and unknown classifications; untrusted tool descriptions cannot downgrade operation risk.

features.name: File access protection
acceptance: Enforce read/write root, extension and classification policy on the actual file operation, including canonical paths and symlinks.
Test traversal, symlink replacement, hardlinks, nonexistent targets and platform differences; argv inspection alone is not filesystem enforcement.

features.name: SQL query firewall
acceptance: Use dialect-aware parsing and parameter handling for operation, table, column and resource policy; never use regex alone as a SQL parser.
Reject multi-statement, comment, CTE, encoding and dynamic-SQL bypasses; test real database execution permissions and tenant isolation.

features.name: Shell command security
acceptance: Add parser-backed executable and argument policies; reject ambiguous constructs and shell expansion unless an explicitly supported sandbox handles them.
Test interpreter flags, command substitution, pipelines, redirection and executable changes without claiming command parsing is process isolation.

features.name: Process isolation integration
acceptance: Provide at least one qualified OS/container sandbox adapter with filesystem, network, resource and process-tree limits; publish a capability matrix for other backends.
Prove kill escalation, descendant cleanup, timeout enforcement, secret isolation and unavailable-sandbox fail-closed behavior on supported platforms.

features.name: Credential delegation
acceptance: Delegate short-lived, narrowly scoped credentials from an external issuer or vault to authorized tool execution without exposing master secrets.
Bind credentials to principal, tenant, task, audience and expiry; test revocation and verify secrets never reach prompts, logs or approval displays.

features.name: Resource ownership enforcement
acceptance: Resolve ownership through a trusted application/provider interface before resource-specific side effects and bind the resource version where required.
Fail closed on missing, stale or cross-tenant ownership; cover confused-deputy and check/use races with integration tests.
remaining: Run actual Dvar runtime, full package build and supported Node/ESM/CommonJS consumer qualification.
Qualify real authenticated issuer/session providers, canonical subject mapping, revocation and remote transport failure behavior.
Integrate authority checks at MCP, stdio, Mayura/framework and direct-workflow boundaries; unwrapped references remain outside this opt-in wrapper.
Qualify production ownership backends and executor-side atomic tenant/owner/version conditions; preflight rechecks alone do not close check/use races.
Add cross-process evidence/delegation integration, benchmarks and independent adversarial/security review before verification.

features.name: Transaction-aware authorization
acceptance: Authorize an explicitly bounded multi-step transaction with allowed resources, amounts, sequence and expiry.
Test partial execution, replay, cancellation, changed transaction payloads and compensation; do not imply arbitrary external side effects are atomic.

features.name: Agent identity and trust levels
acceptance: Establish application-verified agent identity, roles, tenant, issuer and trust attributes independently of model-generated arguments.
Reject forged, missing and stale identity evidence; audit the verified source and keep Dvar separate from an identity provider.
remaining: Run actual Dvar runtime, full package build and supported Node/ESM/CommonJS consumer qualification.
Qualify real authenticated issuer/session providers, canonical subject mapping, revocation and remote transport failure behavior.
Integrate authority checks at MCP, stdio, Mayura/framework and direct-workflow boundaries; unwrapped references remain outside this opt-in wrapper.
Qualify production ownership backends and executor-side atomic tenant/owner/version conditions; preflight rechecks alone do not close check/use races.
Add cross-process evidence/delegation integration, benchmarks and independent adversarial/security review before verification.

features.name: Agent-to-agent authorization
acceptance: Authorize each inter-agent request against both caller authority and callee policy, preserving the attributable delegation chain.
Test cross-tenant calls, agent impersonation, cyclic delegation and context loss across process boundaries.

features.name: Delegated authority limits
acceptance: Intersect child capabilities with parent grants, resource scope, tenant, expiry and budgets; children cannot broaden inherited authority.
Test privilege amplification, detached children, forged ancestors, excessive depth and delegation-chain revocation.

features.name: Task-scoped permissions
acceptance: Issue and enforce task-bound grants with exact resources, capabilities, expiry and revocation reference.
Reject reuse in another task, principal, tenant or environment and verify task completion closes remaining authority.

features.name: Agent behavioral baselines
acceptance: Maintain tenant-separated baselines for tool sequence, volume, resources and destinations using privacy-safe telemetry.
Provide cold-start behavior, reviewable thresholds, drift monitoring and adversarial tests for poisoning and false positives.

features.name: Adaptive risk scoring
acceptance: Combine attributable deterministic risk signals into versioned, explainable scores and escalation rules.
Ensure risk scoring never overrides an explicit denial or expands authority; test missing signals and monitor-to-enforce calibration.

features.name: Action-chain analysis
acceptance: Evaluate stateful sequence policies across a task, including read-export-upload combinations and prohibited transitions.
Test interleaved agents, concurrent steps, evasion by renaming actions, state loss and TTL expiry without leaking data between tenants.

features.name: Kill switch
acceptance: Revoke permission for new actions by agent, principal, tenant or deployment with bounded propagation and attributed administration.
Test in-flight versus new-action semantics, disconnected stores and recovery; do not claim already committed external effects can be undone.

features.name: Agent execution leases
acceptance: Require renewable, signed or store-backed execution leases bound to task, identity, resource scope and expiry.
Test lease expiry, clock skew, stale holders, reconnects and revoked renewals using fencing where external systems support it.

features.name: Workflow security policies
acceptance: Apply policy to workflow entry, transitions, retries and completion with durable workflow identity and step correlation.
Test resume, replay, cancellation and independent workflow dispatch paths rather than relying only on agent tool hooks.

features.name: MCP 2026 specification support
acceptance: Implement the reviewed MCP 2026-07-28 contract with version negotiation/migration boundaries, required routing headers and stateless request validation.
Run the official supported SDK/conformance scenarios and reject header/body disagreement; document legacy 2025-11-25 behavior explicitly.

features.name: Multi Round-Trip Request security
acceptance: Bind additional input requests and responses to the original MCP action, authority, scope and expiry.
Re-evaluate changed actions and reject replayed, cross-request or unauthorized continuations, including user-confirmation substitutions.

features.name: Dynamic tool visibility
acceptance: Filter tools/list according to verified caller policy without weakening execution-time authorization.
Preserve pagination and protocol validity; test tenant-specific caches, stale listings and direct calls to hidden tools.

features.name: Continuous MCP integrity monitoring
acceptance: Revalidate inventories on a configurable schedule and supported change notifications, with reviewable drift and atomic lockfile promotion.
Test metadata/schema expansion, concurrent scans, revoked trust, outages and propagation before subsequent tool execution.

features.name: MCP server trust profiles
acceptance: Define versioned, attributable profiles for trusted, third-party, unknown and high-risk servers with explicit least-privilege defaults.
Test profile transitions and unknown servers; a server cannot self-assert trusted status via its descriptions or annotations.

features.name: MCP OAuth security
acceptance: Validate issuer, resource/audience, scope and credential binding per the reviewed protocol and authorization standards.
Test discovery SSRF, redirect/mix-up attacks, token leakage and downstream audience confusion; never blindly forward a caller token.

features.name: MCP response streaming guard
acceptance: Parse and filter supported streamed MCP responses with correct event framing, request correlation and JSON-RPC error semantics.
Test fragmented events, malformed frames, cancellation, reconnects and batch isolation; enabling output policy cannot leave an SSE passthrough.

features.name: MCP tool execution analytics
acceptance: Expose per-server/tool usage, denial, cost, latency, error and approval metrics with bounded labels and tenant authorization.
Test event correlation, duplicated delivery, redaction and missing outcome handling without exporting raw payloads by default.

features.name: MCP supply-chain verification
acceptance: Verify supported publisher identity, package signatures and provenance against explicit trust roots and reviewed artifacts.
Reject digest/signature mismatch, rollback and untrusted publishers; surface unsupported verification as unknown rather than trusted.

features.name: Data classification engine
acceptance: Apply configurable public/internal/confidential/restricted labels from trusted rules or classifiers with evidence and inheritance.
Test nested data, ambiguity, unknown types and user attempts to lower a label; keep classification separate from model assertions.

features.name: Sensitive data tracking
acceptance: Propagate classification and provenance through declared tool inputs, outputs and workflow steps without retaining raw sensitive content by default.
Test transformed, combined and cross-agent data as well as concurrency; declare untracked opaque transformations instead of assuming declassification.

features.name: PII detection and redaction
acceptance: Provide configured structured detectors and redactors for common PII, credentials and domain-specific identifiers.
Test multilingual formats, false positives, nesting, arrays, primitive outputs and encoded content; document detection limits and external DLP integration.

features.name: Output schema enforcement
acceptance: Validate output contracts before disclosure and revalidate rewritten output using bounded schema processing.
Test primitives, arrays, circular/unsupported values and redaction-induced invalidity; external schema references must not trigger uncontrolled fetches.

features.name: Streaming DLP
acceptance: Maintain bounded detector state across byte/UTF-8/chunk boundaries and withhold undecided content before disclosure.
Test split secrets, incomplete suffixes, buffer exhaustion and cancellation; define bounded lookahead and fail-closed handling for unsupported detectors.

features.name: Content provenance
acceptance: Attach attributable source labels for tools, documents, services and users with separation of trusted control metadata from untrusted text.
Test spoofed origins, label preservation, document-to-tool propagation and redaction without leaking identifiers across tenants.

features.name: Prompt-injection risk signals
acceptance: Produce reviewable signals for suspicious tool responses and MCP metadata without treating model-based detection as an authorization guarantee.
Test multilingual/encoded/indirect instruction patterns and false positives; deterministic authority limits remain enforced when detection misses.

features.name: Data export restrictions
acceptance: Evaluate classified data against the destination, resource ownership, approved purpose and applicable export permissions before egress.
Test read-export-upload chains, redirects, transformed output and cross-tenant destinations; unknown classification cannot silently become public.

features.name: Custom output processors
acceptance: Expose ordered, typed sanitizer/classifier hooks with bounded execution and explicit trust requirements.
Test processor failure, timeout and mutation; processors cannot override a prior denial or leak raw content to telemetry.

features.name: Approval dashboard
acceptance: Build an authenticated, tenant-isolated reviewer UI that displays exact action, resources, changes, scope, expiry and history.
Test reviewer authorization, XSS in tool-supplied content, CSRF, concurrency and audit privacy; no approval based only on a free-text summary.

features.name: Slack and Microsoft Teams approvals
acceptance: Implement both workplace approval integrations with verified platform callbacks and mapped authorized reviewers.
Test forged, replayed and expired interactions, channel/tenant confusion and secret redaction without allowing chat text to grant authority.

features.name: Multi-person approval
acceptance: Support explicit quorum and separation-of-duties rules with distinct authorized reviewers bound to one immutable action.
Test duplicate approvals, self-approval restrictions, changed actions, concurrent votes and expired/revoked quorums.

features.name: Approval delegation and escalation
acceptance: Route pending approvals to eligible delegates or escalation groups under bounded time and authority rules.
Preserve quorum and separation of duties; test absence, expiry, re-routing loops and identity changes.

features.name: Approval fatigue protection
acceptance: Deduplicate exact pending requests, rate-limit approval storms and surface scope expansion clearly to reviewers.
Test grouping without semantic conflation, adversarial flood, broad-grant warnings and preservation of exact action bindings.

features.name: Emergency revocation
acceptance: Revoke approval grants, agent authority and tool access across instances with attributable administrative actions and bounded propagation.
Test race with execution, cached grants, disconnected instances and recovery; define already-executed action limitations.

features.name: Python SDK and runtime
acceptance: Provide a real Python distribution implementing the shared action/policy contract and supported execution boundaries.
Run cross-language golden vectors for canonical hashes, decisions, grants, quotas and error modes; document deliberately unsupported features.

features.name: Native Mayura adapter
acceptance: Qualify the Dvar-backed Mayura firewall package as a single-install integration with native permissions/budgets preserved.
Test real Mayura tool, workflow, direct invocation, approval, output and cancellation paths; raw-proposal and validated-input boundaries must not diverge silently.

features.name: LangChain/LangGraph adapter
acceptance: Provide native adapters for both supported LangChain tool execution and LangGraph workflow boundaries with verified context mapping.
Run real SDK consumer tests for allow/deny/approval/output, sync/async/streaming calls, resume and interruption behavior.

features.name: Additional framework adapters
acceptance: Qualify named integrations for Mastra, LlamaIndex and OpenAI Agents SDK rather than declaring support through structural types alone.
Maintain pinned compatibility tests, supported-version policy, cancellation and approval/output conformance for every advertised adapter.

features.name: Policy presets
acceptance: Ship reviewed starter policies for support, coding, finance and infrastructure agents with explicit authority and monitor/enforce guidance.
Include allow/deny/approval fixtures, tenant boundaries and safe secret handling; examples must validate against the actual policy schema.

features.name: Policy simulator
acceptance: Simulate representative workflows, stateful controls and policy differences without invoking real tools or mutating production state.
Provide deterministic explain traces and counterexamples from actual evaluation; test that dry runs never consume approvals or production quotas.

features.name: VS Code extension
acceptance: Ship a functional editor extension with schema completion, policy diagnostics, rule navigation and deterministic explanations.
Test extension packaging and trusted-workspace behavior; opening a policy must not execute tools or disclose secrets remotely.

features.name: Policy migration tools
acceptance: Provide versioned dry-run migrations with explicit diffs, backup/rollback guidance and unsupported-policy diagnostics.
Test semantic-preservation fixtures and refusal of lossy migrations without acknowledgment; no silent broadening of permissions.

features.name: OpenTelemetry integration
acceptance: Emit correlated agent/action/tool/approval/output spans and bounded metrics through standard exporters with privacy-safe defaults.
Pin the supported semantic-convention version; test Dhal trace correlation, exporter failure isolation, redaction and cardinality limits.
remaining: Execute real OpenTelemetry SDK/exporter and TypeScript consumer tests; local contract harnesses are not SDK qualification.
Run full runtime, public package ESM/CommonJS and supported Node matrix qualification.
Qualify Dhal shared-parent correlation in an actual application, not only a W3C parent-context fixture.
Add granular approval/output operation spans and qualify MCP, stdio, framework and distributed trace boundaries.
Measure overhead, sampling and exporter failure/recovery under load; independent privacy/security review remains outstanding.

features.name: Security analytics dashboard
acceptance: Build a tenant-authorized dashboard for denials, risky tools, approval latency, runtime limits and policy/inventory drift.
Test RBAC, privacy, pagination, filter integrity and degraded telemetry; display missing data rather than invented sample statistics.

features.name: Distributed enforcement hardening
acceptance: Implement atomic multi-control reservations, idempotency, bounded state and recovery for real Redis and Valkey deployments.
Run concurrency, partition, reconnect, clock-skew, replay and crash tests; document consistency guarantees, no-double-charge behavior and safe degraded modes.
remaining: Run full runtime and built-package qualification and the supported Node matrix.
Execute real Redis and Valkey server tests; qualify partitions, reconnects, failover, clock behavior, crashes and recovery.
Extend quota-only atomic admission to remaining stateful controls, execution ownership and distributed approval-use stores.
Benchmark partition contention/capacity; qualify persistence, eviction policy and safe legacy-state migration.
Independent adversarial review and explicit release sign-offs remain outstanding.
